job.title: Governance, Risk & Compliance Program Manager
job.description:
A hyperscale data centre developer and operator with campuses across APAC is building out its ICT function, and this is one of the first senior hires in a new GRC vertical.

You'll own governance, risk and compliance across the data centre OT and ICT estate: building management, power and cooling controls, monitoring platforms and the corporate systems that sit around them. The immediate priority is ISO 27001 alignment and certification, alongside the Australian requirements that apply to critical data centre assets, such as the SOCI Act and Essential Eight.

This is a build, not a maintenance job. There is no GRC platform in place yet, so you'll recommend one, implement it and use it to map, monitor and report controls across the business.

Why it's worth a look

  • A genuine greenfield remit: you'll shape the function, the platform and the team
  • An APAC role at a business with significant capacity planned across the region
  • A hiring manager with a clear, mapped team plan and further hires to follow

What you'll do

  • Set the GRC strategy, roadmap and operating model for data centre OT and ICT
  • Lead ISO 27001 alignment and certification, plus the country-specific controls that go beyond it, starting with Australia
  • Select and implement a GRC platform, and build the control library, testing and reporting on it
  • Own the OT and ICT risk register, risk acceptance and remediation tracking
  • Lead internal and external audits and customer assurance requests
  • Set vendor and third-party security expectations, including remote access
  • Report clearly on risk posture and control maturity to the executive team
  • Lead an assistant manager and direct outsourced specialists

What they're looking for

  • Significant GRC, technology risk or assurance experience in data centres, critical infrastructure, utilities, telecoms, financial services or similar regulated environments
  • Hands-on ISO 27001 implementation, ideally taking an organisation through certification
  • A working knowledge of Australian requirements such as the SOCI Act and Essential Eight
  • Experience building controls on a GRC platform such as ServiceNow IRM, Archer or OneTrust
  • Exposure to OT, building management or industrial control environments is a strong advantage; deep SOC or security engineering experience is not the core of this role
  • The ability to explain technical risk to senior, non-technical stakeholders

job.title: Senior Manager, OT Solutions Architect
job.description:
A hyperscale data centre developer and operator with campuses across APAC is hiring a senior OT Solution Architect, based in Australia, where most of its build programme sits.

This is a hands-on OT role. You'll own the architecture for the systems that keep the data halls running: BMS, EPMS, SCADA, DCIM, PLCs and controls, and how they sit on the underlying IT network. You'll also make sure the platforms and vendors chosen meet the organisation's security and governance standards.

It's a senior individual contributor role. You won't run an internal team, but you will direct outsourced specialists, integrators and technology partners, so technical credibility and influence matter more than headcount.

What you'll do

  • Own the target architecture and standards for data centre OT: BMS, EPMS, SCADA, DCIM, PLCs, controllers and monitoring
  • Define how OT platforms connect to enterprise IT and the network, with resilience and supportability built in
  • Assess vendor platforms and appliances, and set requirements for vendor connectivity and remote support
  • Provide architecture assurance on new builds, expansions and upgrades through design, commissioning and handover
  • Plan lifecycle, obsolescence and resilience across OT platforms
  • Brief senior leaders on OT risk, investment priorities and trade-offs

What they're looking for

  • Hands-on senior experience with BMS, EPMS, SCADA and OT controls in data centres, critical infrastructure, utilities or industrial environments
  • Solid underlying IT and networking knowledge: routing, switching, firewalls and remote access
  • Experience directing vendors and integrators through design, commissioning and handover
  • OT cyber security knowledge, such as IEC 62443 or segmentation design, and GRC exposure are a plus
  • Certifications such as GICSP, CCNP or IEC 62443 are useful

Why it's worth a look

  • You'll set the OT architecture standard for a large build programme rather than inherit someone else's
  • It sits where data centre engineering, controls and IT meet
  • A newly structured ICT team with a clear plan and investment behind it

job.title: Regional Commercial Manager
job.description:
Regional Commercial Manager | Data Centers | Southeast Asia

Our client is a specialist contractor serving the data center market across Asia. They’re looking for a Regional Commercial Manager to oversee the commercial performance of multiple data center projects across Southeast Asia, taking responsibility for cost management, contracts and project profitability across the regional portfolio.

This role calls for someone with a strong grounding in quantity surveying and cost management, backed by substantial commercial and contracts experience. You’ll take responsibility for profitability across the regional portfolio, support project commercial teams, and lead negotiations on major contracts and commercial issues.

You’ll need to be comfortable challenging a cost forecast in detail, then stepping back to advise senior management on the region’s wider commercial position.

The Role
You’ll oversee the commercial lifecycle across multiple concurrent projects, from tender review and subcontract procurement through delivery to final account settlement. Working closely with pre-construction and project leadership, you’ll make sure each project has a sound commercial strategy and that risks are identified and addressed early.

A key part of the role will be setting clear standards for project teams, strengthening cost control, and giving senior management an accurate view of performance across the region.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Taking regional responsibility for project commercial performance, including margins, cash flow and financial exposure.
  • Leading and supporting QS and commercial teams across multiple projects, reviewing forecasts and challenging assumptions where needed.
  • Overseeing cost planning, CVR reporting and cost-to-complete forecasts, with clear reporting at both project and regional level.
  • Leading commercial and contractual reviews of tenders, main contracts and key subcontracts, ensuring obligations and risks are understood before commitments are made.
  • Setting procurement strategies and supporting negotiations with specialist subcontractors and suppliers.
  • Overseeing contract administration, including notices, variations, claims and extensions of time, through to final account agreement.
  • Acting as the senior commercial contact for clients and delivery partners, leading negotiations and resolving escalated commercial issues.
  • Working with pre-construction teams to test pricing assumptions and ensure bids reflect delivery requirements and contractual risk.
  • Improving commercial procedures and reporting consistency across Southeast Asia.

What You Bring

  • A strong QS and cost management foundation, with 12+ years of relevant construction experience and at least 5 years in a senior commercial management or leadership role.
  • A track record of overseeing the commercial performance of multiple major projects, ideally across Southeast Asia.
  • Significant experience in data centers, mission-critical construction or complex MEP projects, with a good understanding of technical fit-out and white space delivery.
  • Strong commercial and contracts experience, including contract negotiation, administration and the resolution of claims or disputes.
  • Detailed knowledge of cost control and forecasting, with the ability to interrogate project accounts and identify financial exposure early.
  • Experience leading QS or commercial teams and working confidently with senior client representatives and internal directors.
  • A degree in Quantity Surveying or a related discipline. MRICS or an equivalent professional qualification would be an advantage.
  • The judgement to balance commercial protection with practical project delivery, and the confidence to challenge decisions when profitability is at risk.
